text:
maria gonzalez: heads up — p99 token-latency on the token-sli/grafana dashboard jumped ~2x in us-west-2 around 09:04 UTC, tokens/sec also dipped. looks like routing churn to fallback-small.
kevin cho: saw that. any correlation with burst autoscaler events or recent shard reshuffle? :thinking:
aj: checking autoscaler logs now, one node pool was drained for image rotate at 09:00, but we have rolling capacity. attaching quick promQL I used:
```
# p99 token latency by region+shard (5m window)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, shard))
```
sam park: that query is expensive with shard cardinality — we need a recording rule for region+shard pxx buckets, otherwise grafana panels time out.
olivia: agreed — also seeing a noisy series from a single hotshard (shard=hot-43) that's responsible for most of the delta. token/sec for hot-43 dropped ~40% while other shards steady.
sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-187 — token-p99-us-west2-spike; assigned to eng-infra oncall.
june liu: if hot-43 lost KV cache locality then TTFT will spike. can we confirm KV cache metrics? query:
```
rate(kv_cache_miss_total{shard="hot-43"}[1m])
```
maria gonzalez: good call. KV cache miss rate did spike right before the routing change. looks like a noisy NIC on the host where hot-43 was landing.
kevin cho: NIC errors would explain retry/backoff and token/sec drop — do we have a rote fallback rule that sends requests to fallback-small when p99 > threshold? that's causing cost change since fallback-small uses slower quantized models.
aj: we do. current routing: policy = prefer-low-latency -> if p99 > 500ms for 2/5m then route to fallback-quantized. but threshold flaps during transient network noise.
sam park: proposed fixes:
- add recording rules: region_shard_token_p50/p95/p99 to reduce panel query cost
- add short-term smoothing (1m) to routing decisions to avoid 1-sample flaps
- create alert that detects single-shard noise by looking at shard_entropy / top_n_contrib
- schedule nic replacement for host in hot-43's node pool
olivia: +1. also suggest limit high-cardinality labels in alert conditions (group by region not shard) and only escalate to paging when >3 shards affected.
june liu: operational runbook notes:
- if token-p99 spike correlated to single shard and token/sec drop for that shard only -> mark shard as hot, cordon node, migrate shard and drain node for NIC tm.
- if multiple shards across hosts -> scale up reserved capacity and fallback route to dedicated-small for critical customers.
maria gonzalez: who can own implementing recording rules and smoothing? I can take recording rules, kevin can own routing debounce.
kevin cho: will add a 90s debounce in router and add a metric `routing_debounce_active` for observability. i'll open a PR later today.
aj: i'll file infra task to add recording rules and test dashboard load. putting a note to limit cardinality with `topk(10, ...)` in panels as temporary stopgap.
sam park: I'll schedule node replacement with infra ops. tagging @ops to confirm maintenance window.
sre-bot: note: alert flapping suppression enabled for token-p99 alerts (1m) per auto-tune, see runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/token-sli
maria gonzalez: thanks everyone — let's target hotfix for routing debounce + recording rules by EOD. I'll update the incident and close when node replaced and dashboards stable. :thumbsup:
